item.description:
Montclair Robotics is a 100% student-led high school robotics team that participates in FIRST Robotics Competition. The team has over 80 student members who spend months designing, building, programming, and promoting a 125-pound robot. The team prides itself on creating an inclusive environment where there are no tryouts or prior required skills. No student is turned away if they are unable to pay their dues. In addition to learning engineering skills, gain leadership experience, build confidence, and participate in community outreach events. The team needs to raise $50,000 each season to cover robot parts, competition fees, transportation, food and more. item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Nov 25, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.description:
This is a free Adult School class.
Rod Serling wrote a few stories for The Twilight Zone about the holiday spirit and specifically, about Christmas. Born on December 25th in 1924, Rod was known to often say, ”I came as a present unwrapped.” Though Rod was Jewish, he and his family enjoyed celebrating Christmas among friends and neighbors in his hometown of Binghamton, NY.
Two of his wonderfully creative holiday episodes will be presented and discussed in the upcoming micro-marathon.
The first is entitled, “The Night of the Meek”: S2:E11 A downtrodden, drunken department store Santa angers his employers and is fired from his job. He wanders aimlessly in the streets of the city until he finds a magic sack that is filled with gifts that can fulfill everyone’s wish, including his. Art Carney is stellar as the Santa Claus that finds his “True North”.

item.title: Amedeo Modigliani: Bohemian of Montmartre and Montparnasse — Wed Dec 2, 1:30 PM — Montclair Public Library
item.description:
This is a paid Adult School class. You can register here.
Amedeo Modigliani, painter and sculptor, was born in Italy to a middle class, cultured Jewish family. He spent most of his tragically short life in France among the avant-garde artists of bohemian Paris. He is known for portraits and nudes in a contemporary style characterized by the elongation of faces and figures. Come and hear about this quintessentially unconventional artist and see many of his ravishing paintings and expressive sculptures. Some of his works are featured in the outstanding upcoming exhibition at the Brooklyn Museum, From Cezanne to Modigliani.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: The Fall St. James Chamber Music Concert — Sun Nov 15, 4:00 PM — St. James Episcopal Church
item.description: St James Episcopal Church is excited to announce that this coming Sunday November 15th at 4PM it will host a chamber music concert featuring the renowned violinist Naoko Tanaka, along with 10 other esteemed musicians. Ms Tanaka will be performing “The Lark Ascending” by Ralph Vaughan Williams. Also on the program are works by Bach, Poulenc, Persichetti, Beethoven and Dvorak. Naoko Tanaka has given concert tours as a soloist and chamber musician in the U.S., South America, Europe, Asia and Canada. A former member of The Theater Chamber Players of The Kennedy Center and The Orpheus Chamber Orchestra, she is a current member of the New York Philomusica and serves as concert master of St Luke’s Chamber Ensemble. She is on the faculty at the Juilliard School, Brooklyn College Conservatory of Music, and The Aspen Music School during the summer. She has recorded for Deutsche Gramophone, Columbia Records, and Music Masters. St James Episcopal Church is at 581 Valley Road in Upper Montclair.

item.description:
We invite you to join us for a Death Cafe in the garden. Seating will be provided, but feel free to bring a blanket if want to sit on the grass.
